sections.title: Basic Concept of Figure Series
sections.content: In Figure Series, a sequence of images is given in which a certain rule is applied to each subsequent figure. Step 1: Carefully observe the first two figures. Step 2: Identify the type of change (rotation, addition, movement). Step 3: Apply the same rule to the following figures. Step 4: Select the next figure according to the same pattern.

sections.title: Simple Rotations
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the main shape in the figure. Step 2: Check whether it is rotating by 45°, 90°, or 180°. Step 3: Identify the direction (clockwise or anti-clockwise). Step 4: The next figure follows the same direction and angle of rotation. Example: If an arrow rotates 90° clockwise each time, the sequence will be Up → Right → Down → Left.

sections.title: Addition or Deletion Pattern
sections.content: Step 1: Count the number of lines or shapes in each figure. Step 2: Observe whether a new line or element is being added or removed in each step. Step 3: Check whether the pattern is consistent. Step 4: Identify the next figure using the same rule. Example: If one new line is added in each step, the figure will gradually become more complex.

sections.title: Moving Element Pattern
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the small element inside or on the edge of the main figure. Step 2: Observe the direction in which it moves in each step. Step 3: Identify the sequence of corners or edges. Step 4: Determine the next position following the same order. Example: A dot may move clockwise around the four corners of a square.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Deciding the rule by observing only one figure. 2. Misidentifying the direction of rotation. 3. Ignoring that addition and movement can occur together. 4. Overlooking small elements in the figure.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Figure Series, the most important step is identifying the type of change. Common patterns include rotation, addition, or movement of elements. Comparing 3–4 figures usually helps in identifying the correct rule quickly.

tricks.title: Identify Rotation Direction
tricks.explanation: Observe the first two figures to see in which direction the shape is rotating.
tricks.example: If an arrow moves from Up to Right, it indicates a 90° clockwise rotation.

tricks.title: Lines Count Method
tricks.explanation: Count the number of lines or shapes in each figure.
tricks.example: If the first figure has 2 lines, the second has 3, and the third has 4 → the pattern is +1 each step.

tricks.title: Corner Movement Rule
tricks.explanation: A small element often moves along the corners.
tricks.example: A dot may move from top-left → top-right → bottom-right.

tricks.title: Clock Pattern Check
tricks.explanation: If the movement is circular, think in terms of a clock direction.

tricks.title: Element Focus Trick
tricks.explanation: Focus on small elements rather than the entire figure.
tricks.example: A small dot may be changing its position in each figure.

tricks.title: Identify Addition or Deletion
tricks.explanation: Observe whether new lines are being added or existing ones removed.
tricks.example: A new triangle may be added in each step.

tricks.title: Two Step Comparison
tricks.explanation: Compare not only the first and second figures, but also the first and third.
tricks.example: This can reveal the complete rotation pattern.

tricks.title: Shape Orientation Rule
tricks.explanation: If the shape remains the same but its direction changes, it indicates a rotation pattern.
tricks.example: An L-shape may rotate 90° in each step.
